# agentgateway_traffic_tcp_route (Resource)

Manages a TCP traffic route: the backends that agentgateway serves for raw TCP traffic on one or more gateways.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A TCP route attached to a TCP gateway. The gateway's TCP backend host is a
# single "host:port" string.
resource "agentgateway_traffic_tcp_route" "postgres" {
  name      = "postgres-backend"
  gateways  = ["postgres-proxy"]
  namespace = "default"
  rule_name = "postgres"

  hostnames = ["db.example.com"]

  backends {
    host = "postgres.example.com:5432"
  }

  # TCP-level policies. A TCP route accepts backendTLS only; HTTP policies such
  # as cors and authorization are not available here.
  policies_json = jsonencode({
    backendTLS = {
      hostname = "postgres.example.com"
    }
  })
}

# A route that points at a backend defined in the gateway's top-level backends
# list. `host` and `backend` never combine.
resource "agentgateway_traffic_tcp_route" "analytics" {
  name     = "analytics-backend"
  gateways = ["postgres-proxy"]

  backends {
    backend = "analytics-primary"
  }
}

# Weighted service backends: 80% of new connections go to the primary database
# and 20% to the replica. The service name is the `<namespace>/<hostname>`
# string the gateway resolves from its top-level services list.
resource "agentgateway_traffic_tcp_route" "replicated" {
  name     = "postgres-replicated"
  gateways = ["postgres-proxy"]

  backends {
    weight = 80

    service_json = jsonencode({
      name = "default/postgres-primary"
      port = 5432
    })
  }

  backends {
    weight = 20

    service_json = jsonencode({
      name = "default/postgres-replica"
      port = 5432
    })
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The route name. Changing it renames the route in place.

### Optional

- `backends` (Block List) Destinations of the route. Exactly one variant may be set per backend. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--backends))
- `gateways` (List of String) Gateways that serve this route, as `<gateway>` or `<gateway>/<listener>`. The server defaults to `default`.
- `hostnames` (List of String) Hostnames served by this route. Wildcards are allowed; unset serves all hostnames.
- `namespace` (String) Namespace of the route.
- `policies_json` (String, Sensitive) Route-level policies as JSON.
- `rule_name` (String) Rule name used by authorization policies.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The route name, which is also the server-side id.
- `revision` (Number) The server revision of the stored route.

<a id="nestedblock--backends"></a>
### Nested Schema for `backends`

Optional:

- `backend` (String) Name of a backend defined in the gateway's top-level backends list. Exactly one backend variant may be set.
- `dynamic_json` (String) Dynamic backend as JSON (`{target: <CEL expression>}`). Exactly one backend variant may be set.
- `host` (String) Backend address as `host:port`, for example `postgres.example.com:5432`. Exactly one backend variant may be set.
- `json` (String) Any other backend as JSON (`aws`, `internal`, `routeGroup`). Typed keys (`weight`, `host`, `backend`, `service`, `dynamic`, `policies`) are rejected inside `json`; set them as the sibling attributes. Exactly one backend variant may be set.
- `policies_json` (String, Sensitive) Policies that apply to this backend only (a TCP backend accepts `backendTLS`) as JSON. Sibling of the backend variant, not a variant itself. Typed backend keys are rejected inside `json`; set them here or on the sibling attributes.
- `service_json` (String) Service backend as JSON (`{name: "<namespace>/<hostname>", port: <port>}`). Exactly one backend variant may be set.
- `weight` (Number) Relative weight of this backend. The server default is `1`.
